roles.title: Change Management Intern (Summer 2027)
roles.description: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the NPI Team The New Product Introduction (NPI) team moves hardware design changes and brand-new products from concept development through large-scale production and commercial use. We coordinate across design, testing, supply chain, quality, manufacturing, and field operations to ensure products are ready to build, launch, and scale in support of Zipline’s mission. About The Role This role on the Change Management/NPI team will help us level up our ability to process and implement changes at high volume and high change velocity. Zipline’s unique ability to quickly improve our hardware and develop new designs allowed us to launch our hardware so successfully, and this role with unlock our ability to expand across the United States and beyond while maintaining the same design improvement velocity. What You'll Do Build a tool that visualizes hardware changes over time, shows how product configurations evolve, and highlights hardware capabilities at specified timestamps. Build a tool that evaluates configuration compatibility across current and previous hardware revisions and summarizes hardware capabilities for specified configurations. Build a user interface for submitting engineering changes that standardizes required information, reduces errors, and generates complete change summaries for technical and non-technical audiences. What You'll Bring Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, computer science, information systems, data science, or a related technical field. Demonstrated experience through coursework, personal projects, research, student organizations, or prior internships building software, data, dashboard, or automation tools. Familiarity with at least one technical tool or language used to build solutions, such as Python, JavaScript, SQL, APIs, spreadsheets, databases, or low-code application platforms. Strong analytical and systems-thinking skills, with the ability to understand relationships, dependencies, and business rules within complex, multi-level assemblies or product data. Ability to gather requirements from users, ask clarifying questions, and turn ambiguous problems into clear workflows, visualizations, or user-friendly interfaces. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document information, explain technical outputs to non-technical audiences, and incorporate feedback from technical and non-technical stakeholders. Detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to validate data, manage changing priorities, and work independently and collaboratively on complex projects. What Else You Should Know This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from May/June to August/September. Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position. The hourly rate for this internship is $40 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period. roles.title: Market Research Intern – Summer 2027
roles.description: Come join one of America’s fastest-growing insurance companies. Since 1848, National Life Group has aimed to keep our promises, providing families with stability in good times and in bad. Throughout that history, we have provided peace of mind to those families as they plan their futures. Our mission extends beyond the insurance and annuities policies that we offer. We strive to make the world a better place through our grants from our charitable foundation, paid volunteer time for our employees, environmentally sustainable and healthy workplaces, and events that promote the work of nonprofits in our own backyard. We foster a collaborative environment with opportunities for growth and encourage our associates to live our values: Do good. Be good. Make good. Please note that we do not offer visa sponsorship for this position POSITION SUMMARY: The National Life Group Internship Program was developed to provide real workplace learning and growth opportunities for undergraduate students. Over the years the program has provided students with the opportunity to engage in meaningful, career-relevant work at National Life Group in preparation for full-time employment. This position currently offers an onsite work schedule, with the expectation that you are in the office four (4) days per week during onsite core days. Our current onsite core days are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday. The work schedule type and core days are subject to change with advance notification and manager discretion. RESPONSIBILITIES: The Market Research Intern will support projects focused on consumer insights, market sizing, and sales trend analysis. This role provides an opportunity for an undergraduate student to gain hands-on experience working with real business data to inform strategic decisions. The intern will collaborate with cross-functional teams including marketing, distribution, strategy, and product to help uncover insights about customer behavior, market opportunities, and business performance. This position is ideal for a student interested in applying analytical and research skills in a business setting. Assist in analyzing consumer data (customer demographic data, survey data, qualitative interview data) to identify trends and insights Support market sizing and segmentation analyses to evaluate growth opportunities across products, markets, and customer segments Analyze sales performance data to identify trends, drivers of performance, and areas for improvement Help develop presentations and reports that communicate insights clearly to stakeholders Conduct competitive and industry research to inform strategic initiatives Partner with team members to translate data into actionable business recommendations Support ad hoc research and analytics projects across marketing and strategy teams QUALIFICATIONS: Preferred Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Economics, Statistics, Data Analytics, or a related field Strong analytical and problem-solving skills Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word Ability to interpret data and communicate findings clearly Strong attention to detail and organizational skills Effective written and verbal communication skills Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment Minimum Experience with data analysis tools (e.g., Advanced Excel functions, Tableau, Power BI or R) Familiarity with market research methods (surveys, interviews, focus groups) Interest in financial services, insurance, or consumer behavior Prior internship or project experience involving data analysis or research AI Proficiency Expectations At National Life Group, we view AI as an enabler of human potential. We use AI to help us work smarter, serve more clients, and keep our promises, while remaining a relationship-driven business where our people are our greatest strength. All associates are expected to: Leverage approved AI tools, where appropriate, to improve the efficiency, quality, and impact of their work. Stay curious and open to new AI-enabled ways of working. Exercise sound judgment by reviewing and validating AI-generated content. Maintain accountability for the accuracy, quality, fairness, and integrity of work products by adhering to National Life's AI guiding principles. Use AI responsibly and in accordance with company policies related to confidentiality, data privacy, security, compliance, retention, and intellectual property. Core Competencies Service Focus - Demonstrates a client centric focus for satisfying one’s external and/or internal customers; establishes and maintains effective relationships with customers and gains their trust and respect. Decision Making - Makes sense of complex information, critically evaluates, and creates solutions. Results Oriented - Sets performance and personal goals; Driven to meet or exceed goals and objectives. Plans and Aligns - Plans and prioritizes work to meet commitments aligned with organizational goals; Aligns people and skills to tasks and assignments; Evaluates results of work. Demonstrates Learning Agility - Enhances skills and knowledge through continuous learning; Focuses on personal results by establishing stretch goals; Seeks feedback and changes accordingly. Establishes Relationships - Builds partnerships with others to instill trust, collaborate, and meet shared objectives. Communicates Effectively - Actively listens, conveys messages to meet different audience needs, and remains open to new ideas and opinions. Fosters Diversity - Values diversity and difference in thought, experience, and perspective; Promotes an environment that embraces diversity, equity, and inclusion; Supports equal and fair treatment for all. HOW YOU SHOW UP: Highly reliable, engaged and possess a customer service attitude Demonstrate effective communication to various areas of the organization (technical and non-technical) Bring creativity, thought leadership, and curiosity to the table; actively participate in forums to contribute and learn Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, i.e. a problem solver’s mindset Eager to learn, ask relevant questions, seek new knowledge, and make connections Enjoy taking on challenges and working towards solutions both collaboratively and independently PROGRAM HIGHLIGHTS: 10-week paid internship (June 1 - August 6) with formal orientation and onboarding Networking opportunities with peers and leaders throughout the summer Cross-Departmental group project focused on an enterprise-wide solution presented at company-wide event Presentation skills coaching sessions Learning opportunities throughout program Access to mentors (former program participants) Base Pay Range . The base pay range for this position is the range National Life reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for the position taking into account the wide variety of factors, including: prior experience and job-related knowledge; education, training and certificates; current business needs; and market factors. The final salary or hourly wages offered may be outside of this range based on other reasons and individual circumstances. Additional Compensation and Benefits . The total compensation package for this position may also include a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits (including 401(k) eligibility and various paid time off benefits, such as vacation, sick time, and parental leave), dependent on the position offered. The successful candidate may also be eligible to participate in National Life’s discretionary annual incentive programs, subject to the rules governing such programs. If hired, the employee will be in an "at-will position" and National Life reserves the right to modify base salary (as well as any other discretionary payment or compensation or benefit program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, company or individual department/team performance, and market factors. National Life is accepting applications for this role on an ongoing basis and the role remains open until filled. Hourly Pay Range $19 — $28 USD National Life Group® is a trade name of National Life Insurance Company, Montpelier, VT – founded in 1848, Life Insurance Company of the Southwest, Addison, TX – chartered in 1955, and their affiliates. Nonclinical Discovery & Development Sciences (NDDS)-2027 Summer Intern
roles.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. **Position Summary** Bristol Myers Squibb’s Nonclinical Discovery & Development Sciences (NDDS) organization is seeking undergraduate students for a 10-week, full-time summer 2027 internship. Each intern is assigned a hypothesis-driven project in a discovery- or development-facing function, with possible areas including target and candidate toxicity, AI and bioinformatics applications, pharmacokinetics, bioanalytical method development, formulation and drug delivery, and laboratory animal welfare. Depending on the project, interns perform laboratory work, literature and data review, programming, and computational analyses with manager support. Interns also develop skills in critical thinking, risk/benefit assessment, and scientific writing, participate in mentoring and cross-functional networking, and present their findings at the end of the program. **Key Responsibilities** -Directly contribute to assigned project with manager support, which is aligned with NDDS responsibilities and student experiences/goals. -Actively participate in mentoring and informal networking meetings, formal symposiums, and cross-functional discussions with Research team members to learn about roles across the drug discovery and development pipeline. -Present overall project and scientific findings at the conclusion of the internship. **Qualifications & Experience** -Undergraduate student, enrolled in an academic program for the Fall of 2027, with demonstrated interest and effort within biology, chemistry, toxicology, computational sciences, pharmaceutical sciences, material sciences, biomedical engineering, veterinary sciences, and related disciplines. -Undergraduate student should have continued interest in pursuing academic endeavors or a career in the sciences after graduation. -Availability for full-time employment (40 hours/week) throughout the 10-week internship period of June 7th to August 13th. **Core Competencies** -Communication: Clear scientific writing and data summarization, plus oral presentation skills for conveying findings to a multidisciplinary audience. -Critical thinking and judgment: Sound reasoning in interpreting data, with attention to detail, accurate documentation, and data integrity. -Adaptability and multi-tasking: Learning new technologies and methods quickly, and managing priorities in a fast-paced environment. -Collaboration and growth mindset: Teamwork across functions, intellectual curiosity, initiative, and receptiveness to mentoring and feedback. We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway. **Compensation Overview:** $24-$30/hour Pay for this internship/co‑op position is provided in accordance with local market practices and applicable laws. Pay may be offered as an hourly rate and/or monthly stipend, or other locally compliant structure. Pay is determined based on objective factors such as academic level, relevant experience, skills, and work location. Interns and co‑op participants may be eligible for limited benefits depending on program structure, work location, and local requirements. Eligibility and offerings are governed by applicable policies and employment regulations. This is a temporary, time‑bound position intended for the duration of the internship or co‑op program and does not guarantee continued or permanent employment following program completion. **How We Work** Where you work matters – because collaboration, innovation and patient impact happen in many settings. Our roles are structured across four work models: site-essential, site-by-design, field-based and remote-by-design. The model assigned to this role is based on its core responsibilities. Learn more at [](https://careers.bms.com/life-at-bms/ways-of-working/) **Supporting People with Disabilities** BMS is dedicated to ensuring that people with disabilities can excel through a transparent recruitment process, reasonable workplace accommodations/adjustments and ongoing support in their roles. Applicants can request a reasonable workplace accommodation/adjustment prior to accepting a job offer. If you require reasonable accommodations/adjustments in completing this application, or in any part of the recruitment process, direct your inquiries to [adastaffingsupport@bms.com](mailto:adastaffingsupport@bms.com). Visit [](https://careers.bms.com/eeo-accessibility) to access our complete Equal Employment Opportunity statement. **Candidate Rights** BMS will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, pursuant to applicable laws in your area. For roles based in Los Angeles County only: If you live in or expect to work from Los Angeles County if hired for this position, please visit this page for important additional information: For roles based in Washington State only: If you live in or expect to work from Washington State if hired for this position, please visit [this page](https://www.atg.wa.gov/fair-chance-act) for important information about the Washington Fair Chance Act. **Data Protection** We will never request payments, financial information, or social security numbers during our application or recruitment process. Learn more about protecting yourself at [](http://careers.bms.com/fraud-protection). Any data processed in connection with role applications will be treated in accordance with applicable data privacy policies and regulations. If this posting is missing required information required by local law or incorrect, contact BMS at [TAEnablement@bms.com](mailto:TAEnablement@bms.com) with the Job Title and Requisition number. Do not send application-related inquiries to this email. To check your application status, please login to your Candidate Home Account. roles.title: People & Culture Intern Summer 2027
roles.description: ABOUT ROCKET LAB Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us. As a People and Culture Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Long Beach, California, you will have the opportunity to gain hands-on experience in People & Culture operations and insight into our company's approach to the employee life cycle. The team collaborates closely with Total Rewards, TA, EIS, Security, Payroll, EH&S, IT, Facilities, and Legal to support daily operations. WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees within the department to apply your knowledge and grow your skills both technically and professionally Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate program in Business Administration, Human Resources, Management or related field and have at least one semester of school remaining post internship. GPA of 3.0 or above. 3+ months of corporate function experience within the areas of Human Resources. THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE GPA of 3.5 or above. 6+ months of corporate function experience within the areas of Human Resources. Strong experience with Microsoft Office (Powerpoint & Excel) Strong time management skills and attentive to details ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning May or June 2027 COMPENSATION AND OTHER BENEFITS Pay Range CA: $25.00 USD Hourly You may be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. Base salary is just one component of our total rewards package at Rocket Lab. Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match. Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts. Eligibility for benefits may vary based on employment status, please check with your recruiter for a comprehensive list of the benefits available for this role. Benefit programs are subject to change at the company’s discretion. Hourly Pay Range (CA Only) $25 — $25 USD WHAT TO EXPECT We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way. Important information: FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY: To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Learn more about ITAR here . This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days. FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY: For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant. roles.title: People Analytics Intern
roles.description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” learn more about working at Coinbase . This is a 12-week internship during summer 2027. You'll join the People Analytics team within our People Success Function. This team provides intelligence and tools that empower leaders to make key people decisions and drive business value. You'll support analyses across the employee lifecycle, help streamline reporting processes, and contribute to solutions that measure the impact of complex People programs. What you'll do: Analyze People data across the employee lifecycle to identify trends and surface actionable insights for leadership Apply AI tools to accelerate data exploration and enable self-service access to insights for stakeholders Prototype AI-driven workflow automations for recurring reports, anomaly detection, and data-quality checks Support ad hoc data requests by building and maintaining spreadsheets and dashboards Partner with stakeholders to improve dashboard navigation, access, and self-service reporting Collaborate with team members to develop executive presentations that translate data into clear narratives Required Skills and Experience: Currently pursuing a degree or certificate in an analytical discipline (e.g., data science, statistics, I/O psychology, business analytics, or related field). Demonstrated experience analyzing and manipulating data using spreadsheets (Excel, Google Sheets) with the ability to translate findings into actionable recommendations. Proven ability to communicate data insights clearly in both written and verbal formats to non-technical audiences. Track record of handling highly sensitive or confidential data with discretion. Familiarity with at least one data visualization tool (Looker, Tableau, PowerBI, or OneModel) or basic SQL knowledge is a plus. Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality Position ID: P78055 #LI-Hybrid Pay Transparency Notice: Depending on your work location, the target hourly rate for this position can range as detailed below. Hourly Rate: $40 — $40 USD Application Limit: Candidates may submit a maximum of 3 applications within a 6-month period. Equal Opportunity Employer: Coinbase is an Equal Opportunity Employer. roles.title: People Operations Intern (Summer 2027)
roles.description: About the role Summer internships will range between the months of May and September depending on university schedules. Internship is full-time and on-site in Mountain View, CA. We’re seeking a self-starting, detail-oriented People Operations Intern . You’ll step into a position where you will learn People Operations fundamentals firsthand and support our day-to-day functions. This position reports to the People Operations Specialist. Interns can look forward to owning a project from start to finish, which could involve building out new people processes, optimizing our onboarding experience, or helping drive key employee feedback initiatives. Come work with the team and help shape the culture and operational foundation for our team members! You’ll thrive in this role if you’re energized by fast-moving environments, enjoy solving problems collaboratively, lead with empathy, and are eager to build a career in People Operations. Muon is a small and fast-growing startup which offers interns the experience to get direct mentorship and have real impact on our programs. As an intern, you'll collaborate with a dynamic team in a startup environment and have the chance to learn from some of the most accomplished and experienced professionals in the industry. We're committed to offering an experience where your decisions and contributions play a pivotal role in driving Muon's success. Responsibilities Provide operational support for broader People Ops initiatives, including team culture efforts. Assist in coordinating a seamless onboarding process for new hires, including managing welcome communications and schedule coordination. Help create, update, and maintain internal wikis, FAQs, and self-serve resources so employees can easily find answers on their own. Build, schedule, and compile feedback surveys (e.g., in Lattice) to help measure and improve the early employee experience. Qualifications Strong organizational skills and sharp attention to detail, ensuring accuracy across administrative tasks and documentation. Strong written and verbal communication skills with an empathetic, warm, and professional approach. High level of integrity and the ability to handle sensitive, confidential information with sound judgment. Tech-savvy and comfortable using Google Workspace, Slack, or HR management software; quick to adapt to new tools and workflows. Ability to prioritize tasks and stay organized in a fast-paced, dynamic startup environment. Nice-to-have Skills Previous internship or co-op experience, or active leadership involvement in campus organizations. roles.title: People Team Summer Intern (Human Resources)
roles.description: About ParetoHealth ParetoHealth is redefining the way employers fund healthcare. As the largest and fastest-growing benefits captive in the United States, we help thousands of small and midsize employers take control of healthcare costs through a smarter, more sustainable model. Our mission is simple: give small and midsize employers the scale and protection they need to eliminate volatility and lower healthcare costs. By combining data-driven insights, innovative risk management, and the collective purchasing power of our community, we enable employers to reduce volatility, improve long-term outcomes, and reinvest savings into their businesses and their people. Headquartered in Philadelphia, ParetoHealth is growing rapidly and transforming one of the country's largest industries. Our success is fueled by talented people who are united by our four core values: Fire in the Belly, For the Greater Good, See the Field, and Get It Done Right. These values shape how we innovate, collaborate, make decisions, and deliver exceptional results for our clients and one another. If you're energized by solving complex challenges, thrive in a high-growth environment, and want to help reshape the future of healthcare, we'd love to meet you. Please note that ParetoHealth does not provide employment visa sponsorship for this position. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship both now or in the future. 2027 Summer Internship Information: Roles will be posted from 11/2/2026 to 12/4/2026. Interviews with the Talent Team and Hiring Manager will be conducted November-January. *Please be sure to apply to the internship(s) which align with your major, your personal interests and desired career path. Thank you! Learn more about our Start Strong Program here: https://paretohealth.com/careers/internships/ Position Summary: The People Team Intern will work closely with the People team to support key programs and operations—from recruiting coordination to new hire training/onboarding and intern programming—and lead projects that improve team processes and future Start Strong Internship classes while gaining exposure to talent sourcing and HRIS. Key Responsibilities: Support recruiting coordination, candidate communications, onboarding preparation, and related administration. Help manage the intern program and coordinate events. Contribute to longer-term projects, including developing standard operating procedures (SOPs) and organizing People team files and data. Support learning and development activities, including new hire training. Analyze broader trends during the internship program to create a peer-led survey, then share findings and recommendations to help shape the Start Strong program for future years. Provide flexible, in-office support for People team activities, events, and day-to-day needs. Gain exposure to talent acquisition sourcing and HRIS functions. Competencies: Work and communicate effectively with colleagues, contribute to shared goals, and value diverse perspectives. Review feedback, data, and trends to develop useful insights and recommendations. Handle records and sensitive People information accurately and responsibly. Coordinate tasks, projects, and events while staying organized and meeting deadlines. About You: You are a Rising Junior or Rising Senior enrolled in an accredited college or university. You are pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree, ideally in Human resources, Business Administration, Organizational Psychology, or a related field. You are available to work in our Philadelphia, PA office from June through early August. We are guided by our values: Fire in the belly The drive to learn, to improve, and to deliver outstanding value every day. See the field The ability to see the big picture and prepare to meet tomorrow’s needs. Get it done right The passion to produce at higher rates and to the highest standards. For the greater good A united community creating better health benefit solutions for all. roles.title: Restaurant Management Internship
roles.description: Hillstone Restaurant Group — Summer 2027 Internship Are you passionate about restaurants, leadership, and creating unforgettable hospitality experiences? Hillstone Restaurant Group invites rising seniors to join our Summer 2027 Internship Program. This internship is a unique opportunity to dive into the world of upscale dining and restaurant management. What to Expect Our internship follows an apprentice-style model , giving you hands-on exposure to every part of restaurant operations. You’ll rotate through key staff-level roles to build a strong foundation in service and daily operations, while also shadowing managers to understand higher-level responsibilities. This immersive experience is designed to help you see what it’s like to be a leader at Hillstone — and to prepare you for a potential full-time Management role after graduation . Details Duration: Summer 2027 Placement: Interns are placed based on best fit across our restaurants nationwide (relocation flexibility required). Compensation: Average of $1,000/week , with variation depending on location. Experience: Prior restaurant experience is helpful but not required — passion, curiosity, and a strong work ethic are what we value most. Why Hillstone? Hillstone Restaurant Group is a privately held collection of some of the most respected restaurants in the country, known for exceptional hospitality, high standards, and strong culture. Our family of restaurants includes: Houston’s, Hillstone, R+D Kitchen, Bandera, East Hampton Grill, South Beverly Grill, Honor Bar, Palm Beach Grill, and White House Tavern. Learn more at or check out our feature in Bon Appétit . Relocation flexibility is required. We place candidates based on best fit. All potential locations are listed on the website. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. The Hillstone Restaurant Group confirms each employee’s identity and authorization to work by participating in E-Verify.

roles.title: Retail Operations Leadership Intern
roles.description: Are you passionate about leadership, operations, and creating exceptional experiences for guests and team members? Pilot Company is seeking ambitious and driven students to join our Field Leadership Academy Internship Program for Summer 2027. This unique leadership development experience is designed for students interested in pursuing a long-term career in retail operations and store leadership. The Field Leadership Academy is a 10-week rotational internship that provides hands-on exposure to Pilot's retail operations while connecting participants with leaders across multiple areas of the business. Through meaningful experiences, mentorship, and structured development, you'll gain firsthand insight into what it takes to lead high-performing teams, drive operational excellence, and build a career path toward Assistant Manager, General Manager, and Field Leadership roles. The program is designed to create a clear pathway from internship to future full-time leadership opportunities within Pilot Company What You’ll Do Participate in a structured 10-week rotational leadership experience across key areas of Pilot's operations. Gain hands-on experience supporting daily store operations, team leadership, guest service, and operational execution. Shadow and learn from store, regional, and divisional leaders to better understand Pilot's leadership culture and business strategy. Explore cross-functional areas including store operations, food operations, Human Resources, and field support functions. Complete a capstone project that showcases your learning and provides recommendations to support business objectives. Build relationships with leaders and mentors who will support your professional growth throughout the internship and beyond. Create an individualized career development and conversion plan focused on future leadership opportunities within Pilot Company. Why Pilot Company? At Pilot, our purpose is to show people they matter at every turn. We believe our future success depends on leaders who can create exceptional guest experiences, build strong teams, and deliver operational excellence. The Field Leadership Academy was designed to help develop the next generation of those leaders by providing meaningful experiences, executive exposure, and a structured path toward future career opportunities. Our culture is built on four core virtues: Driven, Reliable, Authentic, and Welcoming. Throughout the internship, you'll see these values in action while learning from leaders who are committed to your growth and development. This is a full-time, paid, 10-week summer internship hosted in select Pilot markets across the United States. Participants will receive ongoing mentorship, career development support, and a personalized conversion plan designed to prepare them for future store leadership opportunities following graduation Potential Career Path Field Leadership Academy Intern → Store Leadership Opportunity → Assistant Manager Development → General Manager → Field Leadership What We’re Looking For Currently pursuing a bachelor's degree with an expected graduation date within 6 to 12 months following the internship. Strong interest in retail operations, hospitality, business management, or leadership development. Desire to pursue a long-term career in store or field leadership. Demonstrated leadership experience through work, student organizations, athletics, volunteer activities, or other experiences. Strong communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to build relationships across all levels of the organization. Adaptability, initiative, and a willingness to learn in a fast-paced operational environment. Ability to travel within assigned host markets during the internship program. Fuel Discount Nation-wide Medical Plan/Dental/Vision 401(k) Flexible Spending Accounts Adoption Assistance Tuition Reimbursement Flexible Schedule Weekly Pay Pilot Company is an industry-leading network of travel centers with more than 30,000 team members and over 750 retail and fueling locations in 43 states and six Canadian provinces. Our energy and logistics division serves as a top supplier of fuel, employing one of the largest tanker fleets and providing critical services to oil operations in our nation's busiest basins. Pilot Company supports a growing portfolio of brands with expertise in supply chain and retail operations, logistics and transportation, technology and digital innovation, construction, maintenance, human resources, finance, sales and marketing. Founded in 1958 by Jim A. Haslam II and currently led by CEO Adam Wright, our founding values, people-first culture and commitment to giving back remains true to us today. Whether we are serving guests, a fellow team member, or a trucking company, we are dedicated to fueling people and keeping North America moving. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected under applicable federal, state, or local law. Military encouraged to apply.

roles.title: Summer 2027: People Team Intern
roles.description: About Amplify Amplify helps teachers bring delight and rigor to students every day. We have become a leader in K–12 literacy, biliteracy, math, and science by building inspiring teaching and learning experiences based on research. The Amplify Classroom platform combines curriculum, assessment, and supplemental learning into one coherent high-quality instructional system. A pioneer in education since 2000, Amplify has developed deep relationships in states and districts by partnering with educators to drive implementation quality and improved outcomes. Today, Amplify serves more than 18 million students and teachers across all 50 states and on six continents. For more information, visit Amplify.com http://amplify.com. CREATE AN IMPACT BY SHAPING THE WORLD OF EDUCATION! Amplify is seeking a people-centered and organizationally minded People Team Intern to join our team this summer and help us build an exceptional employee experience for the talented individuals who power our mission to deliver innovative educational products to educators, students, and families. This paid, remote 10-week internship offers the chance to make a real impact on products used by millions of students and teachers. If you're comfortable with people operations, organizational dynamics, and human resources principles, and you're genuinely curious about how a thriving workplace culture drives business outcomes, this could be a perfect fit for you. The ideal candidates will love supporting employees at every stage of their journey, bring a collaborative, ask-questions-first energy to your work, and feel excited to help build the inclusive, high-performing culture that moves the needle for K–12 learners. Though remote, interns will join a 2-day in-person experience at Amplify HQ in Brooklyn, NY. Throughout the program, interns will engage with Amplify's culture via product demos, team-building activities, and engagement initiatives, plus grow through a virtual speaker series featuring Amplify executives, additional product demos, and dedicated mentorship. While our summer intern roles are remote positions, interns must be authorized to work in the US, reside in the US for the internship's duration, and be available full-time for the entire program, June 7 – August 13, 2027. Key responsibilities may include: - Support core People Team operations including Talent Acquisition and Onboarding, HR Enablement, and HR systems maintenance to ensure a seamless employee experience - Help identify opportunities to improve people processes, workflows, and programs that enhance employee engagement, retention, and satisfaction - Partner with cross-functional teams to assist with talent acquisition initiatives including job posting management, candidate coordination, interview scheduling, and recruiter support - Contribute to People Team documentation, employee handbooks, HR policy guides, internal communications, and organizational resources - Track and organize people data and HR metrics to help teams identify workforce trends, monitor program effectiveness, and inform strategic decisions WHAT WE CAN OFFER YOU: - Direct exposure to HR tools, people operations practices, and talent strategies used in EdTech - Real-world people challenges that directly impact the employee experience at a mission-driven organization - Collaboration with HR, Talent Acquisition, and Business Operations teams across the organization - Contributions to meaningful culture-building and people initiatives in a fast-growing EdTech environment - Mentorship from industry professionals at the forefront of people operations and organizational development - Exposure to Talent Acquisition, Employee Relations, Learning & Development, Compensation & Benefits, and HR Analytics - Opportunities to help shape the programs, policies, and experiences that make Amplify a great place to work BASIC QUALIFICATIONS FOR THIS AMPLIFY INTERNSHIP: - Education: Current enrollment in an undergraduate degree program, returning to school in Fall 2027 - Full-time availability to participate from June 7, 2027, through August 13, 2027 - Strong written and verbal communication skills - Ability to synthesize information, identify themes, and communicate insights clearly - Knowledge of and interest in the K–12 education technology field PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS FOR PEOPLE TEAM INTERNS: - Working knowledge of HRIS platforms such as Workday, Culture Amp, or similar human resources information systems - Exposure to talent acquisition tools and applicant tracking systems (ATS) such as Ashby, Greenhouse, or Lever - Background in human resources, people operations, recruiting coordination, or organizational development through coursework, volunteer work, or prior experience - Interest in employee engagement, DEI strategy, learning & development, HR analytics, or total rewards - Excellent interpersonal and collaboration skills with the ability to build trusted relationships across all levels of the organization - Comfort with Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace; grounding in data organization, reporting tools, or HR dashboards is a plus Amplify is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Amplify makes employment decisions based on qualifications and merit, and does not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability status, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic or status. Amplify is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities, including disabled veterans. If you have a disability and need an accommodation in connection with the application or hiring process, please email hiringaccommodations@amplify.com. If you are selected for employment, a background check will be required. As required by state and local laws and district policies, you may be required to provide additional documentation, such as proof of vaccination, or submit to enhanced background screening, such as fingerprinting. Amplify is an E-Verify participant.

roles.title: Talent Acquisition Intern
roles.description: ABOUT THE ROLE Prophet is a global brand and growth consultancy helping the world's most ambitious organizations find relevance, unlock growth, and build remarkable brands. Our People team is at the center of that — attracting, hiring, and developing the talent that makes Prophet exceptional. This summer, we're looking for a Recruiting Intern to join us in that work. This is a real seat at the table: you'll support active searches, contribute to how Prophet shows up to candidates and on campus, and help build the programs that keep our intern community engaged from offer to day one. If you're curious about talent, energized by people, and want hands-on experience at a fast-moving consulting firm — this is it. YOUR DAY TO DAY Full-cycle recruiting support Work directly alongside recruiters and hiring managers throughout active searches — from sourcing and screening to interview coordination, offer extension, and onboarding prep. You'll engage with real candidates on real roles. Candidate coordination & pipeline management Schedule interviews, manage candidate communications, and keep records accurate and up to date in Greenhouse, our ATS. A clean pipeline and a great candidate experience are both yours to protect. Intern program & pre-arrival programming Help design and execute the touchpoints, communications, and engagement moments that keep incoming interns excited between offer acceptance and their first day. You'll own pieces of this end to end. Employer branding & recruitment marketing Support initiatives that shape how Prophet is perceived as an employer — from social content and job posting copy to materials for career fairs and campus events. You'll help tell our story to the candidates we most want to reach. Campus recruiting for fall Partner with campus teams to develop recruiting materials and help plan fall events. You'll contribute to how Prophet shows up on campus — content, collateral, logistics, and strategy. Recruiting operations & reporting Help track referral program activity, prepare hiring metrics and reports, and provide project support to the broader Talent Acquisition team as needed. WHAT YOU BRING You're a rising senior pursuing a degree in HR, Business, Psychology, Communications, or a related field You're a strong communicator — comfortable writing professionally and engaging candidates and stakeholders directly You're organized and detail-oriented, able to manage multiple moving pieces without dropping the ball You're curious about talent and people — not just the process, but the why behind it You want ownership, not just exposure — you'll have real deliverables and are excited to run with them Location: New York City Hybrid - 4 days per week in office Salary: $27/hr Please note this internship is only available for rising seniors in college (graduation date of Fall/Winter 2026 or Spring/Summer 2027) Prophet is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. All employment, promotion, and evaluation decisions are based on qualifications, merit and business need.

roles.title: Talent Growth and Inclusion Intern- Summer 2027
roles.description: Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands. Summer Internship Our Summer Internship is designed for students leading into their final year of university, who want to gain real life work experience in a fast past, exciting and professional environment. As a Summer Intern, you will participate in onboarding with the UR team that will set you up for success in your role. You will also benefit from professional development sessions, networking, and social events provided by the Internship Program. The program takes place from June – August 2027 (10-week program). Your Role As a Talent Growth & Inclusion intern, you'll own a meaningful piece of an enterprise-level Talent Management project - spanning career development, performance, learning, inclusion, or leadership development. You'll work directly with the Talent Growth & Inclusion team, People Partners, and subject matter experts. You'll be expected to ask good questions, form a point of view, and present it - not just execute a task list. What you'll do Take a loosely defined problem and turn it into a clear plan: what you're solving, what you need to know, and how you'll get there. Research, synthesize, and structure complex information into something a busy executive can act on. Build presentation-ready deliverables - documents, frameworks, decks, or tools - that hold up without heavy editing. Communicate proactively: flag blockers early, surface what you've learned, and tell us when your thinking has changed. Present your work and recommendations to the team, and to People & Culture stakeholders. What we're looking for Critical thinking. You don't stop at the first answer. You ask why, look for what's missing, and can explain the reasoning behind your recommendation — not just the recommendation. Creative problem solving. You're comfortable when there's no template. You generate options, weigh trade-offs, and try a different angle when the first one stalls. Communication, written and verbal. You write clearly and concisely for the reader in front of you. You speak up in meetings, ask the question you're not sure you should ask, and keep people informed without being chased. You own the outcome, not just the effort. You meet commitments, tell us early when you can't, incorporate feedback the first time, and check your own work before it reaches someone else's desk. How we work with AI We use AI at Veeam every day, and we want you to use it too. But we're specific about how. AI is a tool for extending your thinking — pressure-testing an idea, accelerating research, drafting a starting point, checking your logic. It is not a substitute for it. Interns who thrive here use AI to get further, faster, and can still explain every choice in their work, defend it under questioning, and tell you what the model got wrong. Work that's been outsourced to a model shows immediately, and it doesn't meet our bar. If you're curious about applying AI to make career, learning, and performance experiences more personalized and scalable, you'll have room to run with that here. roles.description: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the Australia Team Zipline is building its presence in Australia, and we are looking for an exceptional student or recent graduate to join the team as a part-time Australia Expansion Fellow. The Australia team is responsible for developing the partnerships, market strategy and operations required to bring Zipline’s autonomous logistics system to communities across the country. This means working at the intersection of business, government, technology and community to understand where Zipline can have the greatest impact and what it will take to get there. The Role As an Australia Expansion Fellow, you will work directly with Zipline’s Head of Australia on our community engagement strategy. This is a hands-on role. You’ll spend time with our local leadership out in the community, meeting residents, businesses and community organisations, listening to their perspectives and ensuring questions and concerns are addressed. You will help translate our exciting but unfamiliar technology into clear, credible and locally relevant conversations. Success means communities hear from Zipline early, have meaningful opportunities to engage with us, and see the benefits of having Zipline operate in their community. The ideal candidate is intellectually curious, an excellent communicator, and highly attuned to community sentiment. roles.title: Change Management Intern (Spring 2027)
roles.description: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the NPI Team The New Product Introduction (NPI) team moves hardware design changes and brand-new products from concept development through large-scale production and commercial use. We coordinate across design, testing, supply chain, quality, manufacturing, and field operations to ensure products are ready to build, launch, and scale in support of Zipline’s mission. About The Role This role on the Change Management/NPI team will help us level up our ability to process and implement changes at high volume and high change velocity. Zipline’s unique ability to quickly improve our hardware and develop new designs allowed us to launch our hardware so successfully, and this role with unlock our ability to expand across the United States and beyond while maintaining the same design improvement velocity. What You'll Do Build a tool that visualizes hardware changes over time, shows how product configurations evolve, and highlights hardware capabilities at specified timestamps. Build a tool that evaluates configuration compatibility across current and previous hardware revisions and summarizes hardware capabilities for specified configurations. Build a user interface for submitting engineering changes that standardizes required information, reduces errors, and generates complete change summaries for technical and non-technical audiences. What You'll Bring Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, computer science, information systems, data science, or a related technical field. Demonstrated experience through coursework, personal projects, research, student organizations, or prior internships building software, data, dashboard, or automation tools. Familiarity with at least one technical tool or language used to build solutions, such as Python, JavaScript, SQL, APIs, spreadsheets, databases, or low-code application platforms. Strong analytical and systems-thinking skills, with the ability to understand relationships, dependencies, and business rules within complex, multi-level assemblies or product data. Ability to gather requirements from users, ask clarifying questions, and turn ambiguous problems into clear workflows, visualizations, or user-friendly interfaces. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document information, explain technical outputs to non-technical audiences, and incorporate feedback from technical and non-technical stakeholders. Detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to validate data, manage changing priorities, and work independently and collaboratively on complex projects. Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period. roles.title: Community Education Intern
roles.description: ABOUT THE CAMPAIGN FINANCE BOARD The Campaign Finance Board is a nonpartisan, independent city agency that empowers New Yorkers to have a greater impact on their elections. Our mission is to make local democracy more open, transparent, and equitable by removing barriers to participation. We make it easier for New Yorkers to vote, meaningfully support candidates for city office, and run for office themselves. NYC Votes, our voter engagement initiative, meets people where they are to share trustworthy election information and help New Yorkers make a plan to vote. We publish the citywide Voter Guide, which delivers information about candidates directly to voters’ doors. Our public matching funds program ensures small contributions can make a big difference, allowing regular people to run for office by relying on the support of other regular people, not just wealthy donors and special interests. And we lift the veil on how candidates raise and spend money, increasing transparency and accountability in local government. We believe that when every New Yorker is empowered to participate meaningfully in elections, candidates will better reflect the communities they serve, elected leaders will be more accountable to the public, and New Yorkers will have a democracy they can truly trust. ABOUT THE UNIT Public Affairs Division The Public Affairs division engages New Yorkers, informs them about elections, and boosts their participation in the democratic process. We make election information accessible and relevant, increase engagement with underrepresented communities, and cultivate a team that reflects our core values of purpose, curiosity, creativity, and collaboration. The division includes, Marketing and Digital Communications, Community Engagement, Language Access, and Public Relations. Our division’s work includes publishing the citywide Voter Guide, running the official citywide Debates Program, and managing the voter engagement initiative, NYC Votes. Community Engagement Unit The Community Engagement unit works to build partnerships across the city to disseminate voting information, deliver accessible voter education, and conduct direct to voter outreach. Through relationships with community-based organizations as well as on-the-ground voter outreach, this team creates pathways for all New Yorkers to gain trustworthy and accessible information and education around voting and democracy. JOB DESCRIPTION The two Community Education Interns will report to the Youth Engagement Specialist and support civic education and engagement initiatives focused on a youth audience. Interns will help develop and deliver educational programming, support youth-focused events and partnerships, and engage young people in learning about voting and civic participation. Specifically, they will lead workshops on topics related to civic engagement and voter information for audiences of high school and college students both within internal youth programming and with external partners. The role will also support the Community Engagement team in building and maintaining strong internal systems to organize and track partnership development. This includes maintaining team databases, documenting outreach efforts, and supporting data entry. The responsibilities and tasks to be completed in this role include, but are not limited to: Community Education and Outreach - Support the development and delivery of educational programming, both internal and external, for a youth audience. - Independently plan and facilitate NYC Votes workshops in a way that engages the audience. - Represent the CFB and NYC Votes at in-person and virtual events. - Register voters and provide non-partisan election information. - Provide administrative support, such as managing email communication, organizing documents, carrying out internal processes, keeping materials organized, etc. - Identify organizations that work in our priority neighborhoods and serve a youth audience. - Support efforts to build relationships with key stakeholders, such as agencies, community-based organizations, schools, and college campuses. - Willingness to learn about best practices for engaging with priority communities. - Support the development and delivery of educational programming, both internal and external, for a youth audience; this includes leading lesson plans for youth ambassadors, leading workshops with external partners, and supporting curriculum development. - Support data entry efforts, including managing and digitizing physical documents, adding information to appropriate digital folders, and helping manage Excel sheets, etc. ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES & OTHER BEHAVIORS (KSAOs) We're seeking individuals eager to make an impact, even if they don't tick every box on our job description. roles.description: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. They are responsible for building and maintaining strong relationships with local government officials, civic organizations, business groups, neighborhoods, and schools. Their work helps individuals and organizations understand the impact of Zipline's service on the community, job creation, and the future of a logistics system that serves all humans equally. The Role Does creating and maintaining important relationships with multiple layers of stakeholders within local communities come naturally to you? Are you an engaging communicator who drives powerful narratives to create excitement and adoption of big and bold ideas? This role is ideal for someone who is passionate about community building, communications, and social impact. You’ll help design and implement strategies to engage our community members, strengthen partnerships, and support outreach initiatives. Support the development of content for newsletters, social media, and other communication channels. Respond to community inquiries and engage with members across platforms. Conduct research on community needs, trends, and engagement strategies. Help track engagement metrics and compile reports on community feedback and outcomes. roles.description: Position Title: Community Organizing and Engagement Intern The Agency You’ll Join: In November 2022, New York City voters overwhelmingly approved three ballot proposals that put racial equity and justice at the heart of city government, including the NYC Commission on Racial Equity (NYC CORE). The first of its kind in the nation, the NYC Commission on Racial Equity is an independent 15-member commission responsible for engaging diverse communities to guide and assess the City’s racial equity planning process. NYC CORE provides accountability for New Yorkers, regularly evaluating the City’s progress on its racial requirements and goals. NYC CORE will be composed of diverse New Yorkers with equity expertise and/or relevant lived experience, serving as a conduit to bring historically excluded communities and voices into government decision-making. The Team You’ll Work With: NYC CORE is an independent commission to hold the NYC government accountable to advance racial equity in government operations and to increase community voice in government decision-making. The Chair & Executive Director is jointly appointed by the Mayor and the New York City Council Speaker. Other NYC CORE commissioners are appointed by the Mayor, City Council Speaker, City Comptroller, and Public Advocate. The Commission's staff is responsible for executing the Commission's day-to-day mission and setting its path to success. NYC CORE team takes the vision of the Chair & Executive Director and the Commissioners and translates it into action strategies and plans that implement accountability for racial equity in the city. Like the Commission itself, the Commission’s staff aims to be representative of New Yorkers from all communities and walks of life. Staff bring an accountability mindset to their work, ensuring they collaborate with city agencies and voice public concerns. The Problems You’ll Solve The Community Organizing and Engagement Intern reports directly to the Director of Community Organizing and Engagement, Cam Morris and the Community Organizing and Engagement team. RESPONSIBILITIES Embeds DEI and racial equity practices and tools into the everyday functioning of the Commission. Monitors and responds to the COE team email for questions, requests, and support needs. Supports team meeting planning, upcoming calendar coordination, and outreach preparation. Preps weekly all-staff updates, coordinates collaboration meetings, and other external meetings as assigned. Sends weekly/biweekly emails to external partners sharing updates and resources. Follow up with community partners on upcoming events and support cross-team collaboration. Support outreach to members for a monthly member highlight in the NYC CORE newsletter. Maintains the COE physical and OneDrive systems by creating an efficient storage process for all COE materials. Track social media feedback, survey responses, general community feedback, and public responses to share with the COE team. Track racial equity news on NYC CORE and mandated areas of focus. Plan logistics, attend external events with the COE team, and follow up with connections for future collaboration. Support with data collection/data entry during the Community Equity Priorities cycle engagement process. Attend outreach opportunities, team meetings, and other team-related tasks based on interests and team needs. Participate in special projects and complete other duties as assigned. About You Commitment to racial equity and seeking a values-aligned role that involves significant creativity and challenge. Community organizing and engagement or customer service experience. An understanding of racial equity, power, privilege, and oppression and how that shapes lived experiences. Some professional experience and at least 2 years of college completed. Background of living in, working within, or growing up as a member of communities facing historical oppression will contribute to your ability to guide the planning process. Demonstrated commitment, competency and strong familiarity with issues affecting Black, Indigenous, Latinx, Asian, Middle Eastern, or Pacific Islander communities in New York City, or other marginalized groups. Demonstrated history of building relationships for your team to enable execution of a strategy that extends beyond the Office. Excellent time management skills and experience working in a deadline-driven environment. Some experience with technical skills, project support, or administrative skills is necessary. Salary The NYC Commission on Racial Equity’s compensation package includes a market competitive salary and exceptional benefits. Our cash compensation range for this role is $18 per hour. Final offers may vary from the amount listed based on candidate experience and expertise, and other factors. If you are an individual with a disability or a veteran with a disability, you may request a reasonable accommodation if you are unable or limited in your ability to access job openings or apply for a job on this site as a result of your disability. Please contact for requests. How to Apply Upload a copy of your resume and cover letter. New York City residency is required within 90 days of appointment. This internship provides exposure to how a large healthcare organization identifies improvement opportunities, evaluates performance, and implements solutions that advance high-quality, safe, efficient, and patient-centered care at either the site-based level or the enterprise level. ​ Key Responsibilities Quality Improvement & Clinical Transformation Support quality improvement and clinical transformation projects focused on improving patient outcomes, safety, care delivery, and operational performance. Assist with identifying opportunities for process improvement and standardization. Participate in project meetings, improvement workgroups, and cross-functional initiatives. Help document current-state processes, identify gaps, and support development of future-state workflows. Research healthcare quality improvement practices and emerging trends to support transformation efforts. Data & Performance Analysis Assist with collecting, organizing, validating, and analyzing quality and performance data. Help monitor key performance indicators and identify trends or areas of opportunity. Develop reports, dashboards, presentations, and visual summaries to communicate findings. Support measurement of project outcomes and progress toward established goals. Translate data and findings into clear, actionable insights for project teams and leaders. Project & Change Management Support project planning, documentation, timelines, deliverables, and status tracking. Assist with meeting preparation, notes, action items, and follow-up. Help develop educational materials, communications, and presentations to support implementation and adoption of improvement initiatives. Collaborate with clinical, operational, quality, analytics, and other teams to support project objectives.
