roles.title: People Operations Associate - Intern
roles.description: Why Work With Us Seven Research is a quantitative research and technology company bringing together exceptional people, rigorous systems, and state-of-the-art resources to solve complex problems in global markets. Our systematic approach emphasizes technical rigor, creativity, and long-term performance. Our people are our core advantage, and as we continue to grow, we are building the operational foundation needed to hire, support, and develop an outstanding team. About the Role We are hiring a People Operations Intern to support the day-to-day execution of our people, recruiting, office, and employee experience functions. This is a hands-on role for someone who is highly organized, detail-oriented, proactive, and excited to learn how to help build a thoughtful, high-performing workplace. You will work closely with our operations team to assist with recruiting coordination, candidate communications, onboarding and offboarding workflows, HR recordkeeping, office operations, vendor coordination, team events, and people-related reporting. You will also help ensure that candidates, employees, visitors, and vendors have a polished, responsive, and professional experience with Seven Research. This is a strong opportunity for someone who wants hands-on experience and broad exposure across HR, recruiting, employee experience, and business operations in a fast-paced environment. What You'll Do Recruiting Coordination & Candidate Experience Support recruiting across technical, research, engineering, and business roles. Help represent Seven Research at career fairs, recruiting events, and talent initiatives. Assist with interview coordination, candidate communications, scheduling, feedback collection, and follow-ups. Help maintain accurate candidate pipeline data in the applicant tracking system. Support recruiting-related communications, including outreach materials, social media posts, and event preparation. Office Operations & Employee Experience Support the day-to-day operations of the New York office. Help manage office supplies, snacks, equipment, mail, meeting room readiness, and general office organization. Assist with coordination across vendors, building management, service providers, and internal stakeholders. Support logistics for internal meetings, team lunches, celebrations, recruiting events, and company programming. Help respond to office-related questions, requests, and logistical needs. People Data, Systems & Process Support Help maintain people, recruiting, onboarding, and office operations trackers. Assist with preparing basic reports related to recruiting activity, headcount, onboarding, events, and office operations. Support process documentation, checklists, templates, workflow improvements, and data quality across HR, recruiting, and office systems. Who You Are You are highly organized, reliable, and detail-oriented. You enjoy creating order, following through, and making sure people have what they need. You are eager to learn, comfortable juggling multiple priorities, and able to communicate clearly while keeping track of details. You are energized by an opportunity that blends people-facing work with operational execution. You are professional, discreet, service-oriented, and proactive about asking questions, taking initiative, and contributing wherever needed. What We're Looking For Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree, or equivalent experience, with an interest in people operations, recruiting, HR, or business operations. Strong organizational skills and excellent attention to detail. Clear written and verbal communication skills. Ability to stay organized across multiple tasks, deadlines, calendars, and stakeholders. Sound judgment and discretion when handling confidential information. Strong follow-through, reliability, and willingness to take ownership of assigned tasks. Familiarity with Microsoft Office tools, especially Excel for data analysis and PowerPoint for presentations. Comfort working with spreadsheets, trackers, reporting, and structured data. Interest in recruiting, HR operations, employee experience, and workplace operations. Professional, polished, and responsive approach to candidates, employees, vendors, and visitors. Previous internship experience or exposure to Greenhouse, HR systems, events, office logistics, or campus recruiting is a plus, but not required. Compensation The base salary range for this role is prorated and based on a full-time salary range of $90,000–$130,000, plus discretionary bonus and benefits. This does not include other forms of compensation and benefits that are part of Seven Research’s comprehensive package. We will provide additional detail about compensation and benefits during our hiring process. Applicant Privacy Please review our Applicant Privacy Notice for information about how we handle candidate information. Accomodations If you need a reasonable accommodation to participate in any part of our application or interview process, please contact careers@sevenresearch.com . We’ll work with you to support your participation. We are an equal opportunity employer and prohibit discrimination and harassment without regard to race, religion, age, sex, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Program details - 12-week paid internship - Generous housing support for those relocating - Daily lunch and dinner in our office - Based at our office in San Jose, CA - Direct mentorship from industry leaders and world-class engineers - Opportunity to work on one of the most important problems of our time For any questions, contact internships@etched.com. internships@etched.com How we’re different Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson http://www.incompleteideas.net/IncIdeas/BitterLesson.html. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system, betting early on transformer and transformer-like architectures and on increasing model sizes. roles.title: People Operations Intern
roles.description: What we’re building The marine industry supports recreation, global commerce, and national defense. And yet it runs on technology that hasn't meaningfully changed in fifty years. Until now. Arc is on a mission to electrify the marine industry. We're rethinking powertrains, software, and vessel designs from first principles. And we're already executing. We started with consumers to develop and harden our core technology. We’re now scaling production of our flagship model with new models and sectors on the horizon. Now we’re extending our platform to commercial applications, starting with tugs, ferries, and defense, with years worth of signed contracts and a pipeline that spans every vessel type on the water. The technology is proven, the momentum is building, and the opportunity is enormous. The marine industry is going electric and Arc is building the platform that powers it Who we’re looking for We’re looking for someone who’s fired up by our mission and ready to build. You’ll thrive here if you adapt quickly, take ownership, and care about the details. You will join our People team as a summer intern from June 14th-August 20th 2027. You will work from our headquarters in Torrance, CA. Given that we’re a startup, you will be working in a fast-moving, dynamic environment that requires adaptability. That said, here are some responsibilities and qualifications we expect to stay relatively constant for this role. What You'll Do Supporting day-to-day operations of the People team and contributing to broader People programs Coordinating and executing process improvement efforts to streamline workflows, such as organizing shared files and team resources so information is accurate and easy to find Developing training content and managing course assignments and completion tracking in EasyLlama Auditing employee records and internal systems for missing, outdated, or inconsistent data, and correcting issues so our records stay clean and reliable Supporting payroll by tracking employee changes, auditing timecards for wage and hour compliance, and coordinating timely manager approvals Preparing compliance paperwork for review, including state disability and family leave forms, wage garnishment orders, and employment verifications, and tracking deadlines through resolution Executing planning and logistics for the company retreat, from vendor coordination and travel to agenda and attendee communications Helping run company engagement efforts, such as scheduling and organizing new-hire lunches with our co-founders and maintaining our employee recognition program Pitching in wherever needed — this is a startup, after all Minimum Qualifications Clear communicator — both written and verbal A systems mindset: you naturally look at ways to simplify, automate and improve processes Hands-on experience using AI tools Highly organized and detail-oriented Proactive problem-solver who thrives in fast-paced environments Proficiency with G Suite and quick to learn new tools Ability to handle sensitive information with discretion and care A genuine interest in People Operations and how organizations work Eagerness to learn and adapt in a dynamic setting. Bonus Qualifications A bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Psychology, Communications, Sociology or a related field, with the ability to start a full time role in September 2027. Experience with HR systems - we use Rippling, Greenhouse and CultureAmp Exposure to startups or small team environments Enthusiasm for boating and clean energy. At Arc, we encourage diversity and consider all qualified applicants equally for employment, regardless of background, identity, or status. You’re always welcome to reach out even if you don’t meet many of these qualifications. Passion and aptitude make up for a lot. What we offer The base pay for this role is $32 per hour. Additionally, Arc offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including: Boat days – Yes, we actually go out on the water. A lot. roles.title: People Ops Intern
roles.description: About The Role Taktile empowers financial institutions to transform into truly AI-native organizations. We're growing rapidly with enterprise customers across banks and insurance companies, and we're looking for an HR Intern to be Taktile's ambassador to our future employees. You will collaborate closely with our People team to ensure the efficient management of the employee lifecycle, from onboarding to ongoing feedback and support. You will play a crucial role in maintaining our HR systems, keeping employee data accurate, and supporting the administrative tasks that keep our people operations running smoothly. By handling these essential tasks, you will contribute significantly to shaping the company's growth and ensuring we maintain a high standard of employee satisfaction and performance. You will work closely with colleagues across all departments to manage various HR activities. What You'll Do as an HR Intern - Employee Onboarding: Once candidates join our team, take the lead in preparing and coordinating first-day agendas for new hires, managing communication to ensure a smooth onboarding experience. - Database and Profile Management: Maintain and update HR-related content on our internal databases and manage employee profiles in our HRIS (HiBob), ensuring all data is accurate and up-to-date. This is crucial for consistency and compliance with company policies. - Administrative Support: Prepare documents for various processes (internal transfers, mobility, etc.). - Employee Benefits Management: Assist in managing and communicating benefits for employees, ensuring they are well informed about their entitlements and processes. - General HR Support: Assist with any HR-related queries, providing timely and accurate information to employees and managers. - Process Improvement & AI Enablement: Help identify opportunities to streamline HR workflows, including building and refining AI tools (e.g. Claude skills) to make our people operations more efficient. About You - Strong time management and multitasking abilities. - Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy. - Collaborative attitude and willingness to assist team members in achieving common goals. - Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English (German is a plus). - Excited to learn about new concepts, tools, and processes and eager to challenge the status quo. Ideal Qualifications (but not required) - Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Psychology, or related field (or equivalent experience). - Familiarity with HR software and tools. What We Offer - Work with colleagues that lift you up, challenge you, celebrate you and help you grow. We come from many different backgrounds, but what we have in common is the desire to operate at the very top of our fields. If you are similarly capable, caring, and driven, you'll find yourself at home here. - Make an impact and meaningfully shape an early-stage company. - Experience a truly flat hierarchy and communicate directly with founding team members. Having an opinion and voicing your ideas is not only welcome but encouraged, especially when they challenge the status quo. - Learn from experienced mentors and achieve tremendous personal and professional growth. Get to know and leverage our network of leading tech investors and advisors around the globe. Our Stance - We're eager to meet talented and driven candidates regardless of whether they tick all the boxes. We're looking for someone who will add to our culture, not just fit within it. We strongly encourage individuals from groups traditionally underestimated and underrepresented in tech to apply. - We seek to actively recognize and combat racism, sexism, ableism and ageism. We embrace and support all gender identities and expressions, and celebrate love in its many forms. We won't inquire about how you identify or if you've experienced discrimination, but if you want to tell your story, we are all ears. About Us Taktile enables financial institutions to transform into AI-native organizations that are increasingly powered by autonomous agents. With our modular Agentic Decision Platform, customers combine AI agents, rules, relevant context, and human oversight to safely automate and optimize their decisions—approving more customers, reimbursing claims instantly, stopping fraud before it spreads, and financing every business worth funding. Founded in 2020, Taktile powers millions of decisions daily for institutions including Mercury, Monzo, Faire, and Pleo. With offices in New York, Berlin, London, São Paulo, and Iași, the company has raised $184M from Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Index Ventures, Tiger Global, Balderton Capital, and Y Combinator. Learn more at taktile.com http://taktile.com. About Your Employment. Taktile operates through regional entities worldwide. Depending on the location of this role, your employment or engagement will be with Taktile LLC (US), Taktile GmbH (Germany), Taktile Ltd (UK), or Taktile SRL (Romania). The applicable entity will be confirmed during the offer process. Your Privacy. Taktile (“we” or “us”) is the controller of the personal data you provide during this application process. We collect and process your name, contact details, resume/CV, work history, education, and any other information you submit or that we obtain from publicly available sources or references. How we use your data. We process your personal data to evaluate your candidacy, communicate with you about the recruitment process, comply with legal obligations (such as right-to-work verification), and, with your consent, to consider you for future opportunities. Legal basis (EU/UK applicants). We rely on (i) pre-contractual steps at your request (GDPR/UK GDPR Art. 6(1)(b)), (ii) legal obligations (Art. 6(1)(c)), and (iii) our legitimate interest in evaluating candidates (Art. 6(1)(f)). Retention. If your application is unsuccessful, we retain your data for 12 months after the recruitment process concludes, unless you consent to longer retention. Successful candidates’ data becomes part of their employment records. Your rights. Depending on your location, you may have the right to access, correct, delete, or restrict the processing of your personal data, to data portability, and to withdraw consent. Automated decision-making. We use automated tools to assist in screening applications. No hiring decision is made solely by automated means without human review. International transfers. Your data may be transferred to and processed in the United States, Germany, the United Kingdom, or Romania. Where required, transfers are protected by Standard Contractual Clauses or other approved mechanisms. By submitting your application, you acknowledge that you have read and understood Taktile’s Applicant Privacy Policy https://taktile.com/applicant-privacy-policy. To exercise your rights or ask questions, contact privacy@taktile.com

roles.title: Preclinical Mathematical Modeling Internship
roles.description: AstraZeneca is seeking a Preclinical Mathematical Modeling Summer Intern to support the Drug Metabolism and Pharmacokinetics, Oncology team within Oncology Research & Development. Based in Kendall Square in Cambridge, Massachusetts, this full-time, dry-lab internship offers an undergraduate the opportunity to contribute to a specialized short-term project supporting capability development or key business initiatives. The intern will review scientific literature, extend an existing modeling framework, and use MATLAB to explore biological mechanisms through ordinary differential equations and parameter sensitivity analysis. # Key Responsibilities - Review relevant scientific literature to inform additions to the current modeling framework. - Develop ordinary differential equations to describe pertinent biological mechanisms. - Perform parameter sensitivity analysis on resulting model outputs. # Required Qualifications - Undergraduate student pursuing Biological Engineering, Biology, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Biochemistry or related engineering majors. - Rising sophomores, juniors and seniors- meeting the applicable graduation timeline requirements with an anticipated graduation date set for after August 2027. - Applied or proficient skills in programming and data analysis. - MATLAB coding proficiency is preferred. - Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team. - US Work Authorization is required at time of application. Applicants must have work authorization that does not now or in the future require sponsorship of a visa. - This role will not be providing CPT or OPT letters of support. - Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills are essential. - Candidates must adhere to the intern program schedule June 7, 2027- August 13, 2027. - Ability to report onsite to Cambridge, MA 3 days a week. This role will not provide relocation assistance. - Hourly range: $37-$39 per hour - #earlytalent **Date Posted** 27-Oct-2026 **Closing Date** 05-Nov-2026 Our mission is to build an inclusive environment where equal employment opportunities are available to all applicants and employees. In furtherance of that mission, we welcome and consider applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of their protected characteristics. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please complete the corresponding section in the application form.

Program Intern, Culture
roles.description: Are you passionate about creating meaningful employee experiences and fostering an inclusive workplace culture? Pilot Company is seeking a Culture Intern to join our team in Knoxville, Tennessee, for the summer of 2027. This is a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience supporting initiatives that shape the team member experience across the organization. You will help analyze industry best practices, identify opportunities for improvement, and contribute to solutions that strengthen Pilot’s people-first culture. In this role, you will be an integral part of our Culture team. Your work will focus on understanding how Pilot’s current programs, practices, and experiences compare to leading organizations while helping develop recommendations that enhance engagement, belonging, onboarding, and overall team member experience. Through research, collaboration, and strategic problem-solving, you will help support initiatives that make Pilot an even better place to work. What You’ll Do Conduct culture and market research: Analyze how Pilot’s current practices compare to external "best in class" organizations and identify opportunities to enhance the team member experience. Support engagement and belonging initiatives: Contribute to projects focused on onboarding, employee engagement, belonging, and experiences designed to support diverse team member populations, including ESL team members. Leverage survey insights: Partner with stakeholders to review engagement survey results, identify meaningful trends, and help develop action-oriented recommendations that improve culture and engagement. Collaborate across teams: Work cross-functionally with business partners to gather information, understand team member needs, and support the implementation of culture-related initiatives. What We’re Looking For Education: Currently pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in Human Resources, Communications, Business, Organizational Leadership, Psychology, or related field. Students from all academic backgrounds with a passion for people and culture are encouraged to apply. Technical Skills: Proficiency in PowerPoint and experience analyzing data and insights from surveys or other feedback sources. Ability to synthesize information and create clear, compelling presentations and recommendations. Soft Skills: Strong initiative, problem-solving abilities, and a results-oriented mindset. Demonstrated executive presence with the confidence to engage with leaders and stakeholders across the organization. Excellent communication, collaboration, and relationship-building skills. Qualities: Passion for philanthropy, volunteerism, and community engagement, with a commitment to fostering a driven, reliable, authentic, and welcoming culture. Why Pilot Company? Our culture is built on four core virtues: Driven, Reliable, Authentic, and Welcoming. As an intern, you'll have the opportunity to contribute to meaningful initiatives that impact team members across the organization while collaborating with leaders who are passionate about creating an exceptional workplace experience. This is a full-time, in-person internship running from June 7 – August 13, 2027. You’ll be working alongside our team in our Knoxville headquarters, where you’ll have the opportunity to build meaningful relationships and experience the full scope of life at Pilot Company. How to Apply If you're ready to take on a challenging and rewarding internship with a leading company, please submit your application. The interview process will include a screening with a recruiter, a 45-minute virtual interview with 2 members of the team, followed by a final round interview with the team's senior leader. We look forward to hearing from you! Pilot Company is an industry-leading network of travel centers with more than 30,000 team members and over 750 retail and fueling locations in 44 states and six Canadian provinces. roles.description: WHO IS LITMUS Litmus is building the data foundation that powers industrial AI. AI doesn’t work without real-world, contextualized data - Litmus makes that data usable. As AI adoption accelerates, most industrial environments still can’t access or use their operational data. We solve that gap. We’re a growth-stage software company helping manufacturers access, structure, and use real-time data from machines, systems, and sensors at the edge. Our platform sits at the intersection of edge computing, AI, and industrial operations, enabling some of the world’s largest companies to run operations in real time, reduce downtime, and optimize production. Backed by leading investors and trusted by global manufacturers and partners like Google, Microsoft, Dell, Oracle, and Mitsubishi, Litmus is powering the shift toward software-defined manufacturing. WHY JOIN LITMUS BUILD THE INFRASTRUCTURE THAT MAKES INDUSTRIAL AI POSSIBLE AI is moving beyond the cloud and into the physical world. At Litmus, you’ll build the infrastructure that enables real-time data to power AI and machine learning systems in production environments. WORK ON PROBLEMS WHERE SOFTWARE MEETS THE REAL WORLD Most AI systems fail without access to real-world data. You’ll build the layer that makes them viable in production. We solve challenges at the intersection of distributed systems, real-time data, and industrial constraints — where reliability, scale, and performance are non-negotiable. HAVE REAL IMPACT, FAST You’ll work on systems used by real customers in production, with direct impact on product and company trajectory. As a scaling company, we move quickly. You’ll have ownership, visibility, and the ability to shape both product and company as we scale. JOIN A HIGH-PERFORMANCE TEAM We’re building a team that holds a high bar and pushes each other to improve. You’ll work alongside experienced operators, engineers, and leaders who have done this before and are building again at scale. We hire people who take ownership, move quickly, and care about outcomes. No passengers. OUR CULTURE At Litmus, the team is collaborative, curious, and low ego. People are scrappy, take ownership, and look for ways to make an impact. We value empathy just as much as execution, whether that’s in how we build, how we communicate, or how we support each other. We’re a growing company, so things move quickly and not everything is perfectly defined. If you enjoy figuring things out, working closely with others, and making steady progress, you’ll do well here. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re hiring a Recruiting and People Ops Intern in Toronto to support our growing global Talent team and People Operations in Toronto. You’ll keep our hiring process running smoothly, coordinate interviews across time zones, and help create a great experience for every candidate. You’ll also learn how to run first-round screens for some roles. A part of this role is learning how to use AI in recruiting and People Ops. You’ll use AI tools to make our processes faster and more consistent, help build automations, and support recruiting and People metrics. If you’re interested in People Operations, there’s also the option to split your time and work on projects with our People Ops team, such as onboarding, employee experience, and HR operations. This is a hands-on role in a fast-paced startup. You’ll get real ownership, learn how a Talent and People team is built, and see the full employee lifecycle from candidate to new hire. WHAT YOU’LL DO RECRUITING COORDINATION - Schedule interviews and coordinate with candidates, hiring managers, and interview panels across time zones - Conduct first-round screens with candidates to assess fit and share notes with the Talent team - Be a main point of contact for candidates, keeping them informed and supported throughout the process - Keep candidate data in Ashby clean and up to date - Help prepare interview materials and make sure interviewers have what they need - Help coordinate pre-hire steps and handoffs to People Operations - Support employer brand projects, such as job postings, career page content, and events AI AND METRICS - Learn to use AI tools for recruiting and People Ops tasks, such as drafting candidate communications, summarizing interview notes, and preparing documents - Help find ways to use AI and automation to improve our recruiting and People Ops processes - Build and maintain recruiting and People metrics, such as time-to-fill, pipeline health, and source effectiveness - Help prepare reports and dashboards for the Talent and People Ops teams - Share what you learn with the team and help document AI workflows and best practices PEOPLE OPERATIONS (OPTIONAL) - Support new hire onboarding, including preparing materials and coordinating first-week schedules - Help maintain employee records and HR documentation - Help with employee experience projects and company events - Support other People Ops projects as they come up WHAT YOU’LL BRING MUST HAVE - Currently enrolled in or recently graduated from a university or college program (co-op applicants must be enrolled in an eligible co-op program) - Strong interest in recruiting, People Operations, or HR - Strong interest in AI and how it can be used to improve the way teams work - Strong written and verbal communication skills, and comfortable speaking with candidates - Very organized and detail-oriented, able to manage multiple schedules and tasks at once - Comfortable working with data and spreadsheets - Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where not everything is defined yet - Curious and eager to learn, with a willingness to take ownership - Able to work in our Toronto office on a hybrid schedule NICE TO HAVE - Previous internship or work experience in recruiting, HR, or a coordination or administrative role - Hands-on experience using AI tools like Claude or ChatGPT - Experience with automation or no-code tools, or building simple reports and dashboards - Familiarity with Ashby - Interest in tech, startups, or AI Location: Toronto, Canada (hybrid) Start Date: Flexible. We’re open to full-time or part-time starting now, or a co-op term starting January 2027.

This is a hands-on opportunity to learn how recruiting teams identify talent, assess potential, engage candidates, coordinate interviews, and create a thoughtful candidate experience. You will work with recruiters, recruiting coordinators, hiring teams, and university or program partners to turn role requirements into focused sourcing strategies. The right candidate is curious, resourceful, organized, and motivated to understand both the people and the work behind each role. What you’ll do Learn Astera Labs’ business, teams, roles, recruiting process, and candidate experience standards through training, shadowing, and hands-on work. Build candidate-sourcing strategies using role-specific keywords, Boolean search strings, research, and approved recruiting channels. Research and identify potential candidates for assigned roles, documenting relevant experience and explaining the candidate-to-role connection. Apply role-specific screening criteria and distinguish must-have qualifications from trainable skills with guidance from the recruiting team. Maintain accurate candidate, outreach, follow-up, and status information in Greenhouse and other approved recruiting systems. Support candidate outreach and follow-up with clear, respectful, and timely communication. Help coordinate interviews, interview materials, scorecards, scheduling, and candidate next steps. Support campus recruiting, career-fair, university, and program-sourcing activities by collecting candidate information consistently and tracking follow-up owners. Partner with recruiters, recruiting coordinators, hiring teams, and cross-functional stakeholders to clarify role profiles, school priorities, sourcing plans, and next actions. Prepare recurring updates on sourcing activity, pipeline quality, follow-up completion, and project progress, including blockers and recommended next steps. Identify gaps in recruiting workflows and develop an adopted process, tracker, or resource that improves team efficiency. Own a defined internship project and present the results, documentation, conclusions, and recommended next steps at the end of the internship. What you bring Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in human resources, business, communications, psychology, sociology, or a related field. Strong research, organization, written-communication, and interpersonal skills. Curiosity about people, technology, and how roles connect to a company’s products and business goals. Ability to learn new systems and processes, manage details accurately, and follow through on commitments. Interest in sourcing, talent acquisition, candidate experience, university recruiting, or recruiting operations. Ability to handle candidate and business information with discretion and professionalism. Comfort asking questions, receiving feedback, solving problems, and working through ambiguity. A proactive, collaborative, learning-oriented approach and the resilience to stay engaged when priorities or sourcing strategies change. Preferred qualifications Experience with candidate research, Boolean search, recruiting, campus organizations, career services, customer service, or other people-focused work. Familiarity with applicant-tracking systems, recruiting workflows, spreadsheets, or process documentation. Experience creating trackers, reports, presentations, or other materials that help a team work more efficiently. Interest in technical recruiting and willingness to learn enough about engineering, product, and business roles to represent them accurately to candidates. Equal opportunity Astera Labs is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage anyone with relevant experience to apply. Internship experience and compensation This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges from $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship. Interns participate in Early Career programming, including technical and professional-development sessions, community events, and an end-of-program project presentation.

roles.title: Refugee Barrier Reduction Intern (Spring 2027)
roles.description: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. SCOPE OF WORK: IRC programming assists refugees to become economically self-sufficient and supports acclimatization within the United States by providing access to casework services. This role will support the IRC’s economic empowerment program in effectively reducing the barriers of humanitarian migrants to achieve self-sufficiency in the United States. RESPONSIBILITIES: Provide clients with support in the completion and submission of various applications to assist the reduction of barriers to employment in the United States (childcare voucher applications, LifeLine phone applications, etc.). Conduct training on the topics of public transportation, childcare options, digital literacy, job readiness, and understanding public benefits to reduce barriers to employment. Participate in supporting clients in Job Application Hours to understand the process of applying for jobs in the United States and submit needed employment applications to achieve economic self-sufficiency. Coordinate with economic empowerment service teams to support clients over the course of their service provision at the IRC in issues of barrier reduction. Engage respectfully with all clients regardless of background. Facilitate and conduct client outings (contingent upon office status) to financial institutions, libraries and various other venues to support client engagement with needed resources. Other duties as identified by Family Employment Services (FES) Program Coordinator. LEARNING OBJECTIVES: Intern will gain insights into IRC casework and workforce programs and the process of refugee and asylee integration within the United States. Intern will learn to communicate effectively with clients across cultures and with interpreters. Intern will learn individual coaching techniques to engage and empower adults. QUALIFICATIONS: Self-motivated and able to work independently Excellent communication and writing skills, including cross-cultural communication skills Works well in a fast-paced environment and adapts quickly to change Strong interest in refugee and asylee issues. Language skills in Spanish, Amharic, Dari, Pashto, Haitian-Creole, French, Kinyarwanda or Swahili are a plus Three-month minimum. Required 24 hours/week. Preferred full-time. Preference to current students and recent graduates* TO APPLY Click Apply Now at the top of this page. Please attach a resume, cover letter and list of (at least) three references to your application. The deadline for applying is 01/04/2027. roles.title: Research Intern (Academic Credit) - Simpkins Lab - Department of Neurology - Per Diem (On-site)
roles.description: About Us: We are a leading research institution committed to advancing scientific knowledge and innovation. Our team is dedicated to conducting ground breaking research and providing meaningful learning opportunities for aspiring scientists. Join us and contribute to our mission while gaining invaluable experience in a dynamic and collaborative environment. The Research Internship program provides students and trainees an opportunity to develop basic research skills. Interns in this program are provided the opportunity to experience and observe many different aspects of basic, translational and/or clinical research. This program offers interns a unique experience, which is intended to provide a wealth of knowledge about the numerous options for a career in healthcare research. Typically lasting not more than a twelve-month period, this internship will expose participants to a diverse spectrum of clinical and non-clinical based research investigations. Under direct supervision from the assigned Postdoctoral Scientist, senior-level Research Associate and/or Principal Investigator, the intern will be provided with basic research instruction, will be oriented to the Institutional Review Board and other Human Subjects courses, and will be introduced to new and innovative research practices and techniques. Overview of Department & Mentor Acute stroke treatment care evolved greatly over the past few years. Imaging, omic's and genetics can reveal patients' clinical trajectory and identify novel therapeutic pathways to develop new stroke and cerebrovascular disease treatments. The goal of this project is to assist in the development of blood biomarkers, MRI, and clinical outcomes database for bioinformatics for cerebrovascular disease. Students will work on projects as part of the Dr. Simpkins lab SkRIPT/CREST, which incorporates team science and career development program for trainees with an interest in stroke. Role Activities & Timeline Role Activities and curriculum (skills to be learned) over the course of 1 year: Literature review 1 month Chart view and redcap entry 7 months Manuscript writing last 3 months Presentation development 1 month Career Development mentorship throughout: CV building Pre-residency neurology prep lectures Presentation skills Basics of project development and critical thinking for research project development Systems Access: N/A Role Summary & Objectives: This internship will provide an introduction to clinical research. The intern will be taught the importance of human subject's protection, HIPAA, research compliance, IRB review. The intern will learn the importance of chart review, keeping accurate and detailed records and logs, data entry, basics of manuscript writing, and data analysis. The intern will also learn basic information about stroke pathophysiology, brain imaging, and neuroanatomy. The intern will work on manuscript writing and statistical analysis. Required Education & Experience: • Must be 18 years of age or older. • Must have a HS Diploma or GED. • Must reside in the greater Los Angeles area or surrounding cities while conducting all activities related to the intern or visitor appointment. • INTERNS: Those participating for academic credit must receive academic credit for the duration of the internship. Preferred Education & Experience: • Undergraduate student. • Basic knowledge of research methods and statistics desirable. • Experience with RedCap, Python, Anaconda, STATA, R Studio, SPSS, or SAS software considered an asset. • Experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and Adobe.

roles.title: Resettlement & Youth Casework Intern (Spring 2027)
roles.description: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. Scope of Work: The resettlement and youth casework teams support refugees and other eligible humanitarian immigrants with their resettlement in the United States. Before client arrival, the resettlement team coordinates arrival logistics for an airport pick-up and prepares housing/furnishing. After arrival, the teams provide a myriad of support services, including culturally orienting them to life in the U.S., connecting them to public school and eligible benefits, and referring them to internal and external providers all with the goal of clients reaching economic self-sufficiency and social integration as quickly as possible. This position will report to a caseworker or youth caseworker. Responsibilities: Assist with home set-ups before client arrival, including lifting, moving, unpacking, assembling, and transporting household supplies, furniture, and food. Support clients by completing applications for eligible public benefits, Medical insurance, social security cards, and more. Orient clients with the local public transit system via conducting bus orientations in the field. Refer clients to external services including but not limited to English classes and medical screenings. Support staff with school-aged youth enrolling in public school, including also accessing technology, school lunches, and the school bus. Assist staff with delivering orientations to school-aged youth and parents on public school, early childhood options, and applying for childcare scholarships. Conduct check-in calls and send messages to clients to determine the status of any unresolved service provision and provide guidance or assistance with the support of the intern supervisor. Research and build community resources to fill any gaps in services, as needed. Record client interactions and service provision in compliance with funder requirements by inputting data into Microsoft Excel and databases. Other related duties as assigned. Learning Objectives: Intern will learn how housing is secured and prepared for newly arriving refugees. Intern will gain professional U.S. field-office experience interacting with and supporting refugee clients, including both adults and school-aged youth with supervision. Intern will acquire detailed knowledge of the programs and benefits available for clients during their resettlement. Intern will learn tracking and reporting requirements per multiple federal and state funders and how capturing this data improves service provision. Qualifications: 22.5 to 37.5 hours per week (3 to 5 full-time days per week) in-person at the IRC office and a four-month commitment. Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle is preferred. Willing and able to transport, lift and move items as needed to set up homes and otherwise support new client arrivals. Proficient digital literacy skills (e.g., Microsoft Excel, Outlook, and Word) and the ability to learn new software and tasks. Organized and attentive to detail. roles.title: Resettlement Case Management Intern ( Spring2027)
roles.description: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. Scope of Work Resettlement case management interns support IRC’s resettlement team with daily tasks that help welcome and promote the self-sufficiency of refugees, asylees, and other humanitarian immigrants in the Baltimore metropolitan area. As the initial point of contact for newly arrived refugees, the IRC’s case management teams provide support, guidance, and continued integration assistance for up to five years after arrival. Interns will work directly with individual clients and families to assist in delivering resettlement services. Reports To Caseworker or Casework Supervisor Learning Objectives Learn about the services that refugees, asylees and other humanitarian immigrants are eligible for upon arrival in the U.S., including public benefits in Maryland and local resources in the Baltimore metropolitan area. Learn about strategies for effective, holistic case management. Develop resourcefulness and problem-solving skills to work independently in different situational contexts. Learn to communicate effectively with clients across cultures. Responsibilities Under the direction of the intern’s supervisor, assist clients remotely or in-person with key services such as housing set-ups, activating EBT cards for food stamps, applying for Social Security cards, or obtaining Maryland ID cards. Assist clients to coordinate transportation to medical and other required appointments. In coordination with the resettlement team, conduct remote, office, home or community-based orientation sessions on topics such as opening bank accounts, using EBT cards at grocery stores, or using public transportation throughout Baltimore. Assist with service documentation through case-notes and case file maintenance. Other duties as assigned. Qualifications Prior experience and interest working with refugees and immigrants preferred. Prior experience and interest in case management or social work preferred. Ability to work independently and as a team member in a fast-paced, cross-cultural environment. Flexible and reliable, with outstanding attention to detail. Strong problem-solving skills. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook) and web-based applications (databases, Box). Fluency in English required. Bilingual ability in one of the predominant languages of the local client base is desired. Valid driver’s license, reliable access to a vehicle with current insurance and the ability to travel regularly throughout Baltimore preferred. Position Details IN-PERSON: Spring 2027 internships will be hybrid. This includes a combination of standard office environment, remote work, and field time within the greater Baltimore area. DATES: Internships start with a required orientation on Wednesday, Jan 27th (approx. 9:30 AM – 3 PM). Regular weekly hours start the week of Jan 27th, 2027, and will continue through May 16th, 2027 (14 total weeks). HOURS: Internships require a minimum of 15 hours per week for 14 weeks. Interns should be able to come to the office at least 3 days per week. LAPTOP: Interns will be issued an IRC laptop for the duration of the internship to perform both remote and in-office responsibilities. REIMBURSEMENT: Internships with the IRC in Baltimore are unpaid. roles.title: Restaurant Management Internship
roles.description: Hillstone’s summer internship is designed for rising seniors with a serious interest in pursuing a career in restaurant management or culinary management. Interns are exposed to the business in its entirety; however, a specific focus is placed on daily operations and service. While the majority of time is spent apprenticing staff-level roles, there is also an opportunity to understand management level functions which can include hiring, training, coaching, inventory management and P&L oversight. Previous experience working in restaurants is helpful, but not a prerequisite. Intern placements will be determined by fit and assigned to an operating team in one of the restaurants around the country, with a strong focus on East Hampton, NY and Aspen, CO. Compensation will vary based on location but typically average $1200-$1800/week. Hillstone Restaurant Group is a privately-held collection of upscale restaurants with 45+ locations in vibrant cities across the country. Some of our more well-known operations are Houston’s, Hillstone, R+D Kitchen, Bandera, East Hampton Grill, South Beverly Grill, Honor Bar, Palm Beach Grill, and White House Tavern. To learn more, visit us at , or read this profile in Bon Appetit magazine: Placement for the internship is decided upon hire, based on fit to the operating team. This might not be in Aspen, CO, as we have 38 properties around the United States, making relocation contingent upon employment. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. The Hillstone Restaurant Group confirms each employee’s identity and authorization to work by participating in E-Verify.

roles.title: Revenue Cycle Management Intern
roles.description: ### About The Role Hi, I'm [Karen Salmon](https://www.linkedin.com/in/karen-salmon-6a3719119/), the U.S. Insurance Lead here at Jane. I've been with Jane for over two years and lead a small but mighty team supporting U.S.-based clinics through the real, day-to-day complexities of insurance billing. Our work is all about helping clinics get paid accurately and on time. We collaborate closely with payers, internal teams, and clinic staff to remove friction, clarify processes, and advocate for our customers. We're launching our first-ever internship program on the US Insurance team, and this is where it starts. As our Revenue Cycle Management Intern, you'll work directly alongside our senior billers, learning the real mechanics of medical billing while helping us keep pace with a growing customer base. If you're studying medical billing, coding, or health information tech and want hands-on experience that actually matters, this is a great place to get it. ### What Impact We're Looking For You To Make - Keep claims moving by following up on outstanding claim statuses and documenting outcomes clearly for the team. - Support accurate, timely payment posting by reviewing ERAs and EOBs under the guidance of your supervising biller. - Bring structure to denial trends by logging and categorizing denials so patterns are easy to spot and act on. - Help patients and clinics stay informed by preparing and maintaining patient statements. - Strengthen the team's knowledge base by keeping internal documentation current and useful for both new hires and daily reference. ### What Experience We Need - Recently completed (or nearing completion of) a Medical Billing & Coding, Health Information Technology, or Healthcare Administration program. We're looking for candidates who are well into their coursework or already graduated, not just starting out. - Familiarity with core revenue cycle concepts like claims, ERAs/EOBs, and denials, whether from coursework, an externship, or hands-on experience. - Comfortable learning new software and tools quickly, and not afraid to ask questions when something's unclear. - Strong attention to detail and follow-through, especially when managing repetitive or detail-heavy tasks. - Able to commit to a consistent Monday-Friday schedule during standard business hours in your time zone, for the duration of the internship. If you don't meet every single qualification but are excited about this role, we'd still love to hear from you. ### More About Jane Jane is a founder-led, high-growth SaaS company with a remote-first team working across Canada, the US, and the UK, united by our mission to help the helpers. We build the products and tools that thousands of clinics rely on every day to run their businesses, care for their patients, and grow their communities. That level of impact means every person at Jane plays an important role in how we show up for our customers. We're all responsible for being deeply connected to their needs, obsessed with improving their experience, and proud of the difference our work makes in their day-to-day lives. Jane is growing fast, and that growth brings exciting challenges that call for adaptability, resilience, learning agility, and humility. We're proud of what we've built and quick to admit what we don't know yet. We listen, learn, and adjust as we go. More than 70,000 businesses run on Jane which has 250,000+ practitioners interacting with our product on a daily basis and growth is continuing to accelerate. Our goal isn't just delivery - it's delight. We move quickly, communicate openly, and solve real problems together. If you're energized by ambiguity, motivated by impact, and eager to learn with others, you'll thrive at Jane. ### Compensation This is a 6-month, paid internship. Pay is set at minimum wage for your specific location, so your exact rate will depend on where you're based. We're aiming for full-time hours, but we're staying flexible as the program gets off the ground - we'll learn and adjust together as we go. This role is fully remote, with an expectation of availability Monday through Friday during standard business hours in your time zone. For the right person, a successful internship could lead to a permanent position on our team, which would include our full benefits package. That said, this depends on both fit and whether we have an opening available at the time, so it's a possibility we're excited about rather than a guarantee. ***Jane takes job scams and candidate fraud seriously.** Jane will only contact you from an @*[**](http://jane.app) *email address. We'll never contact you from a personal email, ask for payment, or request purchases during the hiring process. If something doesn't seem right, please reach out to us at* [*hiring@jane.app*](mailto:hiring@jane.app) *before sharing any personal information.*

roles.title: School Psychology Intern - SY 27-28
roles.description: Two full-time school psychology internship positions are anticipated for the 2027-2028 school year. The Office of Psychological Services is a progressive office providing consultation, assessment, and intervention services to all students, in a large, very diverse suburban school district. The internship is designed to meet standards of the National Association of School Psychologists (NASP) and Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE).

roles.title: School Psychology Internship - 2027 - 2028 School Year
roles.description: School Psychology Internship Applications for full time school psychology internships are now being accepted for the 2026-27 school year. A competitive stipend of $25,000 is offered to the successful internship candidate, along with 10 paid leave days. Only candidates enrolled in NASP-approved/accredited Specialist-level school psychology training programs will be considered for these positions. Applicants should complete an online application with the following uploaded attachments: (a letter of interest, resume, official undergraduate and graduate transcript, recent PRAXIS scores (if available), and three letters of professional reference). Other correspondences may be sent to: Harford County Public Schools Office of Psychological Services 102 South Hickory Avenue Bel Air, MD 21014 As a Harford County Intern, you will: Address the cognitive, emotional, behavioral, and social factors that influence student achievement Support the psychological and mental health needs of students Grow, learn, and have fun in a supportive, collegial environment For additional information, please contact: Sarah Sinclair, 410-588-5282,

roles.title: SG Campus Recruitment - Localization QA (LQA) Intern
roles.description: About Company： As a leading internet technology company based in China, NetEase, Inc. (NASDAQ: NTES and HKEX:9999, “NetEase”) provides premium online services centered around content creation. With extensive offerings across its expanding gaming ecosystem, the Company develops and operates some of China’s most popular and longest-running mobile and PC games. Powered by industry-leading in-house R&D capabilities in China and globally, NetEase creates superior gaming experiences, inspires players, and passionately delivers value for its thriving community worldwide. By infusing play with culture and education with technology, NetEase transforms gaming into a meaningful vehicle to build a more entertaining and enlightened world. NetEase’s ESG initiatives are among the best in the global media and entertainment industry, earning it a distinction as one of the S&P Global Industry Movers and an “A” rating from MSCI. For more information, please visit: http://ir.netease.com/ Position Overview： Responsible for localization quality assurance of the product in overseas target markets, ensuring localized text is accurate, contextually natural, culturally adapted and free of dissonance. The last line of defense for "copy-as-product" quality in overseas publishing. Responsibilities： Conduct language and functional testing of localized versions of in-game text, UI, events and narratives Review translations from a native target-market perspective; correct stiff translations, cultural inappropriateness and tone deviations Log and track localization bugs (text truncation / variable misplacement / encoding issues / contextual errors) Verify text consistency and compliance across language / region versions (e.g., rating language) Coordinate with localization and worldview/narrative teams; provide feedback on how narratives land in target languages Requirements: Currently enrolled or fresh graduate; majors in Language / Translation / Media / Game / Digital Media preferred, any major acceptable Native-level proficiency in target-market languages (English, and/or French / German / Spanish / Portuguese and other European / American languages) Sensitive to target-market culture, slang and gaming terminology Meticulous and patient with strong quality awareness; able to log issues systematically Casual / merge game player experience preferred Preferred Qualifications: Experience in localization / translation / QA / game testing Second or third language proficiency to cover multilingual testing Familiarity with localization tools or bug tracking systems (e.g., Jira) Fair Employment Practices At NetEase, we are committed to fair employment practices. We welcome applications from all individuals, irrespective of age, gender, race, religion, marital status and family responsibilities, or disability.

roles.title: Spring 2027 Talent Acquisition Co-Op (Full-Time)
roles.description: At Keeley Companies, we believe in empowering our people and fulfilling career aspirations. Keeley is a career destination with countless opportunities for advancement, and a world-class family culture that is centered around creating the best possible environment for our people to thrive. We are looking to hire a full-time Talent Acquisition Co-Op for our Corporate Human Resources team in St. Louis, MO starting January 2027. Primary Responsibilities Lead campus recruitment projects including engineering and construction management fall career fair research, swag and storage management, sourcing students on LinkedIn etc. Assist in compiling campus recruitment best practices research and creating recommendations based upon findings. Support Talent Acquisition team with summer intern program events. Schedule meetings, interviews, and assist with HR Communications projects, as requested. Conduct resume screens and phone screens for candidates across various roles and assess candidate fit. Assist with sourcing efforts and build talent pipelines using a variety of tools and our applicant tracking system. Assist the Talent Acquisition and Corporate HR team with projects as needed. Conduct research, compile data, and implement ideas for various assigned projects. Minimum Qualifications In pursuit of a bachelor’s degree in HR, Psychology, Communications, or other closely related degree. Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, and Outlook). Communicate effectively both orally and through writing and work cooperatively in a fast paced, diverse team environment. All candidates agree to complete an assessment for selection and pre-employment drug screen. EOE/AA M/F/Disabled/Vet #LI-AG1 #LI-Onsite All Keeley Brands (Keeley Construction Group, Keeley Properties, Keeley Restoration, Keeley Companies) do not accept unsolicited resumes from search firms, headhunters, or agencies. Any resume submitted to any employee of a Keeley company without a prior written search agreement will be considered unsolicited and the property of any Keeley Company. Please, no phone calls or emails. All Keeley companies are proud to be an equal opportunity employer regardless of race, color, gender, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, religious beliefs, marital status, genetic information, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other basis protected by federal, state, or local law.

roles.title: Spring 2027: Consumer Insights Co-op, Shark (January to June)
roles.description: About Us SharkNinja is a global product design and technology company, with a diversified portfolio of 5-star rated lifestyle solutions that positively impact people’s lives in homes around the world. Powered by two trusted, global brands, Shark and Ninja , the company has a proven track record of bringing disruptive innovation to market and developing one consumer product after another has allowed SharkNinja to enter multiple product categories, driving significant growth and market share gains. Headquartered in Needham, Massachusetts with more than 4,100 associates, the company’s products are sold at key retailers, online and offline, and through distributors around the world. AI at SharkNinja At SharkNinja, we’re building an AI-native culture. We’re not waiting for the future; we’re creating it. Our people are expected to experiment boldly, adopt new tools, and continuously raise what’s possible to create meaningful impact for our consumers. If you believe the best way to do your job hasn’t been invented yet, you’ll fit right in. Work Period: January through June Location & Schedule: This is a full-time, 40-hour-per-week position with a minimum of 3 days per week onsite in Needham, MA . There is no relocation or housing assistance for this position. Compensation Range: Ranges from $28/hr - $34 /hr. Specific compensation is set according to a standardized scale aligned with your educational level at the time of hire. Join the SharkNinja Early Edge Experience: Built for early talent. Geared toward impact. Driven by speed. Whether you're in a co-op or internship, our early talent program is designed to provide valuable exposure to the industry and a fast-paced professional environment. You’ll dive into meaningful projects and tasks that sharpen your skills and deepen your knowledge. Along the way, you’ll benefit from professional development opportunities, community events, and connections that make your experience well-rounded and enriching. Your time with us will culminate in an opportunity to showcase your contributions and learnings to SharkNinja leaders because this is a program for those ready to shape what’s next — fast. This role: Consumer Insights Co-op Are you naturally curious and eager to uncover what drives consumer behavior? Do you thrive at the intersection of data and strategy and have a passion for understanding the category and consumer? Are you interested in shaping 5-star products through research that directly impacts business decisions? If so, we invite you to learn more about the Consumer Insights Co-op role at SharkNinja . As a key member of our Consumer Insights team, you’ll play a vital role in shaping the future of our products through strategic research and real-world impact. You’ll dive deep into both qualitative and quantitative data, uncovering the insights that drive innovation across SharkNinja’s brands. From planning and executing research studies to translating consumer feedback into product opportunities, you’ll gain hands-on experience at every stage of the research process. This is a unique opportunity to sharpen your analytical thinking, flex your curiosity, explore the product journey, and collaborate cross- functionally in a fast-paced, innovation -driven environment. If you're passionate about understanding people, energized by data, and excited to help build 5-star products that solve the unsolvable, we want to hear from you! Here are some of the EXCITING things you’ll get to do: Support and analyze qualitative and quantitative research to uncover trends, insights, and innovation opportunities Assist in developing and executing research plans that drive product and marketing decisions Translate feedback—including unmet and latent needs—into clear recommendations for new products and features Identify whitespace opportunities and customer pain points to guide product strategy Collaborate cross-functionally to plan research and manage timelines and resources Synthesize insights into compelling stories that influence brand, product, and executive strategy Design and refine research tools (e.g., surveys, discussion guides) to support various initiatives Monitor competitors and market trends to inform strategic positioning Help build customer personas and journey maps to guide brand and UX strategy Contribute to brainstorms with insight-driven ideas that fuel innovation Develop a strong understanding of SharkNinja’s consumer-first approach and digital marketing culture ATTRIBUTES & SKILLS: Education: Current student in a related bachelor's or master’s program or has graduated from such a program within the past year Must be able to work a full-time, 40-hour-per-week schedule with a minimum of 3 days per week onsite in Needham, MA . Experience or coursework in market research, consumer insights, psychology, sociology, or related social sciences is strongly preferred Naturally inquisitive, with a passion for uncovering consumer insights and behavioral trends Strong project management and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities Thrives in a dynamic, hands-on, fast-paced environment Approaches uncertainty with confidence and consistently identifies opportunities to contribute Recognizes and responds to the needs and expectations of both internal teams and external stakeholders Ability to synthesize complex data into clear, actionable insights, focusing on relevancy and impact opportunity Cultivates trust and understanding with others by following through on commitments Open-minded and eager to learn from both data and cross-functional perspectives Please note that, due to the high volume of applications for early talent roles, response times may vary depending on the specific role and timeline. Our team appreciates your patience! Salary and Other Compensation: The hourly salary range for this position is displayed below. Factors which may affect starting pay within this range may include geography/market, skills, education, experience and other qualifications of the successful candidate. The Company offers the following benefits for this position, subject to applicable eligibility requirements: medical insurance, health savings account (HSA) with company contribution, sick time, company holidays, employee product discount, product testing opportunities, referral bonuses, and more. Hourly Pay Range $26 — $35 USD Our Culture At SharkNinja, we don’t just raise the bar—we push past it every single day. Our Outrageously Extraordinary mindset drives us to tackle the impossible, push boundaries, and deliver results that others only dream of. If you thrive on breaking out of your swim lane, you’ll be right at home. What We Offer We offer competitive health insurance, retirement plans, paid time off, employee stock purchase options, wellness programs, SharkNinja product discounts, and more. We empower your personal and professional growth with high impact Learning Programs featuring bold voices redefining what’s possible. When you join, you’re not just part of a company—you’re part of an outrageously extraordinary community. To gether, we won’t just launch products— we’ll disrupt entire markets. At SharkNinja, Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion are vital to our global success. Valuing each unique voice and blending all of our diverse skills strengthens SharkNinja’s innovation every day. We support ALL associates in bringing their authentic selves to work, making an impact, and having the opportunity for career acceleration. With help from our leadership, associates, and our community, we aim to have equity be a key component of the SharkNinja DNA. roles.title: Talent & People Strategy Internship (all genders)
roles.description: As Talent & People Strategy Intern at Lio, you will help build the team and people infrastructure behind one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies. Backed by a16z and Y Combinator, we are building a category-defining product and an exceptional team to match. Working closely with the People & Culture team and our hiring managers, you will identify and engage outstanding talent while helping establish the systems and processes that will support Lio as we scale. This isn’t a role where you simply support existing people operations. You will help build them from the ground up. What You'll Do In this role, you will: - Actively identify and approach exceptional candidates, building a strong pipeline of A-players who can shape Lio’s next stage of growth - Take ownership of sourcing projects using LinkedIn Recruiter: from defining target profiles and building searches to crafting outreach that gets responses - Conduct initial interviews, assess candidate motivation and fit, and create an outstanding first impression of Lio - Help implement HiBob and build the foundation of a scalable, data-driven People Operations function - Design and improve people processes across recruiting, onboarding, employee data, and internal workflows - Gain direct insight into people strategy and contribute ideas that help us attract, develop, and retain exceptional talent - Identify opportunities to simplify, optimize, and automate repetitive People processes - Own projects end to end and see the direct impact of your work on our team and growth Your Profile You are a strong fit for this role if you: - Are available for a minimum of four months, starting as soon as possible - Are currently pursuing or have recently completed a degree in business, psychology, human resources, technology, or a related discipline - Have previous hands-on experience with active sourcing and know how to identify and engage strong candidates - Feel confident using LinkedIn and ideally have experience with LinkedIn Recruiter - Bring a strong academic track record and/or have demonstrated exceptional ownership through student initiatives, entrepreneurial projects, or other extracurricular activities - Have native-level proficiency in German and are fluent in English - Are structured, proactive, and comfortable taking ownership without waiting for detailed instructions - Adapt quickly to a fast-paced environment with ambitious goals and changing priorities - Have experience with HiBob or another HRIS WHY JOIN US? At Lio, you won’t just support the People function, you’ll help lay its foundation. roles.title: Youth Tutoring Intern
roles.description: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. NOTE ABOUT COMPENSATION: Internships at the IRC are unpaid. No financial compensation, including compensation for relocation, is available. Reimbursement is available for mileage when using a personal vehicle. Eligible interns will also receive a nominal per diem reimbursement aligned with current intern reimbursement policies. BACKGROUND: Founded in 1933, the International Rescue Committee is a leading, non-sectarian, non-profit organization providing emergency relief, protection, rehabilitation assistance, resettlement services, and advocacy for refugees and victims of oppression or violent conflict. Domestically, our 28 offices across the U.S. ensure new arrivals have food, shelter, and clothing, and work with refugees to help them gain self-sufficiency. SCOPE OF WORK: The Youth Tutoring Intern will support the IRC in Utah’s Education team by implementing the Student Support Volunteer Tutoring Program. This program pairs community volunteers with recently resettled youth in middle and high school to work as a tutor/tutee pair. Pairs meet for at least one hour a week for a minimum of 8 weeks. The intern will oversee day-to-day implementation of the program, including onboarding new volunteers, identifying eligible youth, pairing them, and documenting progress. This is an excellent opportunity for the intern to be directly involved in the implementation of a client-facing program. This internship is ideal for someone interested in teaching, social work, working with youth, or anyone interested in learning how to run a non-profit youth-focused program. MINIMUM COMMITMENT: 10 – 20 hours per week for 10-12 weeks START DATE: January 12, 2027 (final start date to be confirmed) RESPONSIBILITIES: Make phone calls to recently arrived families to identify students interested in the program. Onboard and interview potential community volunteers Complete pairings for new volunteers with eligible students promptly according to demographic and location matching criteria. Coordinate initial meeting times between the student, volunteer, and program supervisor. If available, facilitate the initial introduction meeting between the tutor and student. Document and case note each step of the process in the databases used by the program. Other related duties as assigned, including monthly office support & reception coverage. roles.title: ABA Behavior Technician
roles.description: 🦊 HELP A LOCAL CHILD THRIVE: BEHAVIOR TECHNICIAN Location: In-home or clinic sessions in the Mount Pleasant, MI area Hours: Full-time, M-F 8am-4pm Pay: $17.00 – $22.00 per hour A Little About Us At Finni Health of Central Michigan, we don’t believe in "one-size-fits-all" care. We are a small, heart-led practice that treats our therapists and the families we serve like neighbors. We meticulously personalize care because we understand that each child is unique. We work closely with families to set individual goals and track progress, making adjustments whenever needed. Together, we create a supportive and nurturing environment where our kiddos can thrive and develop vital skills. The Heart of the Role We are looking for someone who doesn’t mind getting down on the floor to play, getting messy with arts and crafts, and celebrating "small wins" like they’re Olympic gold medals. You’ll work one-on-one with a child in the comfort of their own home, helping them learn life skills through the power of play. What your day might look like: - Being a Play Partner: Using a child’s favorite toys or games to help them learn to communicate and socialize. - Building Independence: Helping a child master daily routines that make a big difference for their family. - Cheering Progress: Keeping track of how they’re doing so we can celebrate every milestone together. - Learning Together: You’ll have a supportive mentor (our BCBA) right by your side to guide you. Who You Are You are a compassionate person with a big heart and the right foundation to hit the ground running. - The Training: You have already completed your 40-hour RBT training course. (preferred) - The Next Step: You are ready (and excited!) to sit for your RBT Exam—we’ll provide the support and mentorship to help you cross the finish line. - The Experience: You have a high school diploma and at least a year of experience working with children (especially those with special needs). - The Spirit: You’re reliable, have your own transportation, and are comfortable being active (sitting, kneeling, and playing on the floor). Why You’ll Love Working With Us We know that to take good care of our families, we have to take good care of you. - Consistent Schedule: This Full-Time role is designed to fit into your life. - Support for Your Mind: We offer Mental Health days and Paid Time Off because we know heart-work requires rest. - Family Feel: We offer mileage reimbursement, referral bonuses, and a team that actually knows your name. Ready to meet the family? If you’re looking for work that feels less like a "job" and more like a calling, we’d love to chat. We’re looking for someone who is ready to jump in, have fun, and make a lasting impact here in Mount Pleasant, MI. Apply today—we can't wait to welcome you to the team! Note: To keep our kiddos safe, we require a background check for all new team members. It’s part of our commitment to our families. #FinniHealth2026
